newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel shares close lower in technical correction.
newsitem.headline: Israel shares close lower in technical correction.

text.p: Israeli shares closed lower on Wednesday in what traders said was a much needed consolidation.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares fell 0.68 percent, or 1.78 points, to 258.61 on an all-share turnover of 93 million shekels against 137 million shekels on Tuesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.67 percent lower at 267.00.
"This looks like a correction that might continue tomorrow. The market needs to gain strength before it can resume its rise," said Izik Winish at Capital Securities.

"Investors were taking profits today and the market is very stable at the current level. There is no evidence of selling pressure and most players are optimistic," said Ron Weisberg at IBI Investment House.

"The fact that the market became more selective despite the rise in volume, during the last few days, is a very good sign. It looks good and it is very encouraging that the market is rising slowly, slowly," Winish said.

The most active shares were Blue Square Chain Stores Properties and Investments, which closed unchanged at 3,643 agorot on volume of 4.0 million shekels; Israel Discount Bank, which fell 0.25 percent to 356 agorot on turnover of 3.5 million shekels; and Koor Industries, which lost 1.75 percent to 29,187 agorot on volume of 3.1 million shekels.
